entries.abstract:
Erdős problem 257 asks whether the sum over a in A of 1/(2^a - 1) is irrational for every infinite set A of positive integers. The principal theorem compared here settles the whole reciprocal summable regime at every integer base: if A is infinite and the sum over a in A of 1/a converges, then the sum over a in A of 1/(b^a - 1) is irrational for every integer b at least 2 (ReciprocalSupport.irrational_supportPowerSeries_of_summable_reciprocal). No pairwise coprimality, periodicity, density, or powerful support hypothesis appears. Paul Erdős printed the pairwise coprime case of exactly this statement, at every integer base, in 1968, and stated there that pairwise coprimality can be removed by a longer argument he did not print. The theorem compared here is that stated extension, proved independently. No priority over Erdős is claimed and no identification with his omitted argument is asserted. The consequence for the parent problem is a boundary condition: any infinite support witnessing a counterexample has divergent reciprocal sum. Erdős problem 257 remains open.
The readers are number theorists working on irrationality for Lambert type and reciprocal Mersenne series, and analysts who study subsum sets of convergent series. Erdős (1948) proved irrationality of the full support value at every integer base; Erdős (1968) proved the pairwise coprime reciprocal summable case; Duverney and Tachiya (2019) treated the squarefree support at every base 2^j; Tao and Teravainen proved the prime support case at base two. Duverney and Tachiya record the Erdős and Graham conjecture that the sum is irrational for every increasing sequence of exponents and describe their corollary as support for it. Each covers one distinguished family; none covers an arbitrary reciprocal summable support, nor the reciprocal divergent supports below.
Three theorems state sufficient criteria that do not ask for reciprocal summability. Write h(a) for the P part of a at a finite nonempty prime set P. DivisibilityWeightedSupport.divisibilityWeightedClaim has two clauses: convergence of the sum over a in A of h(a)/(a(b^h(a) - 1)) at a fixed base b at least 2, for infinite A avoiding 0, gives irrationality at that base; the same weighted mass at base two on a host H avoiding 0 gives irrationality at every integer base at least 2 for every infinite subset of H. VariableExponentCover.strengthenedPositiveCoverClaim gives that hereditary all base conclusion for every infinite subset of the host of a positive fractional divisor cover of convergent one inverse power cost, and MixedWeightedCover.mixedSupportClaim combines the two criteria on one observation scale. LiteralWeightedCover.exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host makes the weighted enlargement strict: a weighted host of divergent reciprocal mass admitting no strengthened cover, whose infinite subsets are irrational at every integer base at least 2. DyadicObservationSummability records dyadic averaging estimates for weighted observation masses.
FinitePeriodNoncollapse is exact finite support arithmetic: for finite nonempty F of positive exponents and integer base b at least 2, the reduced denominator of the sum over n in F of 1/(b^n - 1) is coprime to b, the order of b modulo it is exactly lcm F, and lcm F is strictly below that denominator once it is at least 2. RationalTailRigidity adds four necessary conditions on a hypothetical rational value p/(2^c v): an unbounded positive integer tail orbit with exact doubling recurrence, a sublogarithmic bound on zero windows of the divisor incidence coefficients, a reciprocal mass floor from the order of 2 modulo an odd reduced denominator when the reciprocals are summable, and a dyadic mass alternative. None contradicts a rational value. BooleanMobiusCarry gives exact coordinates: for an integer p and a positive natural q, a support avoiding 0 with some positive element and base two value p/q exists precisely when a positive square root bounded integer carry has Boolean Moebius normalised quotient. That characterisation permits finite supports, so it excludes no rational value.
AchievementSetGeometry and FairCoding describe the set of all subsums of that series at base two. For every set J of allowed digit positions the supported coding map is injective with compact nowhere dense range, the range is perfect when J is infinite, and the Lebesgue measure obeys an exact dichotomy: 2^(-|F|) when the omitted positions form a finite set F, and zero when infinitely many are omitted. When 0 is not in J and the value coded by J read as exponents is rational, the supported set is Lebesgue null, which closes positive measure selection over a rational fibre. The fair product measure on digit strings pushes forward to Lebesgue measure restricted to the achievement set, and the preimage of the rationals is null. Perfectness and nowhere density of subsum sets are classical after Kakeya (1914), and Kovac and Tao record the fixed base Cantor structure; the measure dichotomy and the rational fibre null theorem are the additions.
Six families give exact membership criteria for that set. GeneralRepairCriterion replaces a quantifier over supports by a pointwise inequality on one integer sequence: a nonnegative real lies in the set exactly when its greedy defect fails to increase at cofinally many scales, and when it fails to increase inside every window that starts at K and has width 2 times the integer square root of K plus 12. ScaledGreedyTrap identifies the set with the nonnegative reals whose scaled greedy remainder stays strictly below the barrier 2 at every scale. RationalMembership characterises a nonnegative rational target by infinitude of its skipped greedy ranks; PositiveSkipEquivalence and FourNinthsRepairWindows give the criteria at 1/2 and at 4/9; TwentyOneFatalBranch reduces membership of 1/21 to excluding one explicit fatal aligned branch. These are exact reformulations; they decide no target.
TerminalScaledVanishing and ActualUpperSuccessor state conditional refutations of the universal assertion: an unconstructed terminal scaled vanishing sequence of finite Boolean support words, or an unconstructed realised upper run lower envelope, each produces an infinite support of value exactly 1/2. Neither theorem places 1/2 in the achievement set.
Irrationality for an arbitrary infinite support is not proved, the memberships of 1/2, 4/9 and 1/21 are not decided, and the parent problem remains open.
entries.title: Erdős problem #257: all base irrationality of the reciprocal Mersenne subseries for every infinite reciprocal summable support, with weighted mass and positive cover extensions, achievement set geometry, and exact greedy membership criteria

entries.abstract:
The regionally proximal relation and the equicontinuous structure relation are fundamental relations in topological dynamics that capture equicontinuous behaviour in a topological dynamical system and its factors. For minimal actions of abelian groups they are known to be equivalence relations and to coincide. This development formalizes in Lean 4 the results of the paper "The regionally proximal relation for commutative semigroup actions", which generalizes these facts from group actions to semigroup actions.
Throughout, a system is an action of a discrete semigroup S on a compact Hausdorff space X by continuous maps. A factor is a continuous S-equivariant surjection. The system X is minimal if every orbit is dense, and equicontinuous if the family of maps {s : X -> X} is uniformly equicontinuous. The regionally proximal relation RP consists of the pairs (x,y) such that for all neighbourhoods U of x and V of y and all neighbourhoods a of the diagonal, there are x' in U, y' in V and s in S with (sx', sy') in a. The equicontinuous structure relation Seq consists of the pairs identified by every equicontinuous factor.
The regionally proximal relation has classically been defined only for group actions. The definition used here, for actions of a general semigroup, is the one adopted by Auslander and Dai and by Dai and Xiao; it agrees with the classical notion when the acting semigroup is a group. A second, inequivalent generalization is also natural: the backward regionally proximal relation RP^-, obtained by following the group-action definition of de Vries. For semigroup actions the two differ in general, already for S = (N,+), which is what makes Theorem C below a statement with content.
Theorem A states that for a commutative semigroup S and a minimal S-system X, a factor is equicontinuous exactly when RP is contained in the relation it induces. Theorem B states that RP and Seq coincide; in particular RP is a closed, S-invariant equivalence relation and X -> X/RP is the largest equicontinuous factor of X. Theorem B is apparently new even for systems generated by a single non-invertible map. Theorem C states that RP coincides with the backward regionally proximal relation RP^-, the second natural generalization of regional proximality from groups to semigroups; the two differ in general for semigroup actions, already for S = (N,+). Theorem D states that commuting minimal actions of two commutative semigroups on the same space induce the same regionally proximal relation.
Theorems E and F concern natural extensions. Theorem E constructs, for any minimal action of a commutative semigroup, a smallest extension on which the semigroup acts by homeomorphisms: a minimal S-system W and a factor map W -> X through which every extension of X by homeomorphisms factors. The construction goes through the Grothendieck group Gr(S) of S and requires no cancellativity assumption. Theorem F identifies the largest equicontinuous factor of X with that of its natural extension W, both as an S-system and as a Gr(S)-system.
The proof of Theorem B follows the cube-space methods of Glasner, Gutman and Ye, generalized in places and specialized in others, using ultrafilters in place of enveloping semigroups and nets to simplify formalization. The development runs to roughly 20,000 lines of Lean across 17 files and formalizes every lemma, proposition, corollary and theorem of the paper; the registered statements are Theorems A through F. The same repository also formalizes a companion paper on the local structure of Delta* sets, registered separately as Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000015.
entries.title: The regionally proximal relation for commutative semigroup actions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development of two structures of finite-dimensional quantum information, in the vocabulary of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Open Quantum Problems 13 and 23; the fourteen definitions restated character for character under their Apache-2.0 license, see NOTICE). A basis of C^d is a unitary matrix whose columns are the basis vectors; two bases U, V are mutually unbiased when every entry of U^* V has squared norm 1/d; HasMUBs d k says k pairwise unbiased bases exist and IsMaxMUBCount d k that k is the largest such number. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.
entries.title: Finite quantum designs: mutually unbiased bases, SIC-POVMs, and the Welch and Gerzon bounds

entries.abstract: A Lean proof that a discrete matrix representation lifts across a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel exactly when its explicitly constructed second-cohomology obstruction vanishes. The proof constructs the conjugation action and defect cocycle for an abelian group extension, proves the lifting criterion, and applies it to reduction of invertible matrices. The underlying additive kernel is identified with matrices over the coefficient-ring kernel. This is classical obstruction theory motivated by DARPA Challenge 18, not a solution of its homotopy/Langlands research agenda.
entries.title: H2 obstruction to lifting discrete matrix representations

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of results on 3-colourings of planar graphs. (1) Kostochka and Yancey's theorem, the case k = 4 of Ore's 1967 conjecture on the minimum number of edges of k-critical graphs: every finite 4-critical graph G satisfies 3|E(G)| ≥ 5|V(G)| - 2, by their potential method. (2) Grötzsch's theorem: every finite triangle-free planar graph is 3-colourable, deduced from (1) as in Kostochka–Yancey, with the topological crossing argument replaced by a K5-minor argument with an apex inside a face. (3) Aksenov's and Jensen–Thomassen's theorem: a triangle-free planar graph plus one edge is 3-colourable (Borodin–Kostochka–Lidický–Yancey, Theorem 2). (4) A triangle-free planar graph plus one vertex of degree at most 4 is 3-colourable (BKLY, Theorem 4). (5) The Grünbaum–Aksenov theorem: every finite planar graph with at most three triangles is 3-colourable, following BKLY's short proof (Theorem 7), with precolouring extension for 4- and 5-cycles (BKLY Theorem 5, for arbitrary cycles) and a combinatorial region (Jordan-type) theorem for rotation systems making the interiors and outer faces of the paper precise. Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks on this definition K4 is shown planar and K5 and K3,3 non-planar.
entries.title: Grötzsch's theorem, Ore's conjecture for k = 4 (Kostochka–Yancey) and the Grünbaum–Aksenov theorem

entries.abstract: An integral extension of OpenAI's matrix multiplication exponent bound and its previous all-fields extension. The formalization proves that the exact integer coefficient tensor-rank exponent is at most 9/4, yielding division-free arithmetic programs over every associative unital ring, including noncommutative rings. For every positive epsilon, one constant bounds the operation count at all positive matrix sizes by C*n^(9/4+epsilon). The arithmetic model is preserved apart from Field-to-Ring assumptions. The extension uses a primitive tensor spectrum, coefficient extraction, fixed finite-free descent, and coprime patching of Fourier and interpolation constructions. It does not improve the numerical exponent or assert an endpoint O(n^(9/4)) algorithm, efficient uniform generation, or bit complexity.
entries.title: Matrix multiplication: omega at most 9/4 over every ring

entries.abstract: Lean formalization accompanying the paper An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem by Eric Naslund (cited under sources), which proves the exponent 1.043171 unconditionally with a computer-assisted certificate. Conditional theorem on unit distances in the Euclidean plane. Let B = Q(sqrt 241) and let E be the number field of degree 512 generated over Q by sqrt 241 and square roots of the eight elements -1, -71011068 + 4574225 sqrt 241, (-6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, (6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, 31 - 2 sqrt 241, 31 + 2 sqrt 241, 326 - 21 sqrt 241 and 326 + 21 sqrt 241 of B (a basis of the {2,3,5}-units of B modulo squares). Let E_W be the field of degree 8192 obtained from E by adjoining square roots of four explicit elements beta_1, ..., beta_4 of E, each generating with two of the square roots a dihedral extension of B of degree 8 (the elements are written out in the Challenge). Hypothesis (H_W) is one displayed numerical inequality for the Dedekind zeta function of E_W: log(Re zeta_{E_W}(1 + 1/4411))/8192 + (1/4411)((L - gamma - log(4 pi))/4 - Re((zeta_{E_W}'/zeta_{E_W})(2))/8192) < 50969/1000000, where L = (9/4) log 2 + (1/2) log 3615 and gamma is Euler's constant. The compared theorem proves that (H_W) implies the existence of finite sets U_j in the plane with |U_j| -> infinity such that the number of unordered pairs of points of U_j at distance one, divided by |U_j|^(20863/20000), tends to infinity. The exponent is exactly 20863/20000 = 1.04315. The conclusion is a sequence statement only; no bound at every sufficiently large cardinality is asserted. The infinite pro-2 tower over B with Frobenius caps at both primes above 29 and at one prime above 41 (generators, relation bound, presentation, Golod-Shafarevich infinitude, local data), its fields, which are Galois over B and over a fixed base field but not over Q, their local types and signature, the root-discriminant bound, the field E_W with its degree, its embedding in the base field and its local data, the passage from (H_W) to the analytic ceiling, the numerical margin and the planar construction are proved in Lean over Mathlib; (H_W) itself is not proved. Outside Lean, a rigorous computation (certified values of the 576 L-functions of degrees 4 and 8 in the factorization of zeta_{E_W} and an Euler product with explicit tail) bounds the left side of (H_W) by 0.0509172; that computation is not part of the formal proof. The earlier formalization registered as PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000018 version 1 proved the exponent 10427/10000 from a different inequality, for the field E.
entries.title: An Exponent of 1.043 for the Unit Distance Problem: Lean formalization at exponent 1.04315, conditional on one zeta inequality

entries.abstract: This development extends OpenAI's Lean proof of the matrix multiplication exponent bound 9/4 from the complex numbers to every field, including finite fields and fields of positive characteristic. It generalizes Fourier separation and interpolation over each field's algebraic closure, descends tensor powers through one fixed finite coefficient algebra, and connects the resulting exact-rank bounds to the original division-free arithmetic-program model. The compared statements include the arithmetic exponent upper bound, nonvacuity and lower-bound checks, an explicit positive-epsilon operation-count theorem, and exact coordinatewise coefficient decompositions. The original numerical bound and complex-field construction are OpenAI's work; this fork contributes the arbitrary-field extension and its formal verification.
entries.title: Matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4 over arbitrary fields

entries.abstract: Kamenica and Gentzkow's finite-state persuasion theorem from economic primitives: nonempty compact metric actions, continuous sender and receiver utilities, and a full-support common prior. Receiver best replies and sender-preferred tie actions exist. The induced sender payoff is bounded and upper semicontinuous. Finite signals realize exactly finite Bayes-plausible posterior splittings, with prescribed posteriors recovered only at nonnull messages. An optimal finite signal with at most the number of states plus two messages exists and dominates every finite experiment. Its value is the least concave majorant of the induced payoff on the entire belief simplex; strict persuasion gain is exactly the concavification gap. This covers the signal/splitting part of Proposition 1 and Corollary 2, including attainment. The straightforward recommendation branch and compact-state extension are outside this scope. Related finite splitting and abstract attainment are already formalized in Daniel Lyng's Econlib; no first-formalization or novelty claim is made.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Optimal Information and Concavification in Bayesian Persuasion

entries.abstract: In their study of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola–Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems S′ and S′_T, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension T of Peano arithmetic (PA), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in T, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a T-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's S′ is the case T = PA. More generally, for consistent T ⊇ PA, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when T proves every true Π⁰₁ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable T ⊇ PA by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension T ⊇ PA, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if T is Σ⁰₁-sound and the universal relation otherwise.
entries.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition

entries.abstract: Asymptotic correctness of the discriminative Kalman filter for a stationary linear Gaussian state model with nonlinear and non-Gaussian observations. Formalizes Appendix B, Theorem 2, Lemma 1, and Remarks 1–4 of Burkhart et al. (2020): weak convergence, eventual Gaussian well-definedness, L1 consistency, the exact Gaussian parameter update, the robust update, and the extension to random input distributions with convergence in probability.
entries.title: Discriminative Kalman Filter Formalized

entries.abstract: Formalization of 18 claims from manuscript Theorems A, B, C, E (extension direction), F, G, H (hierarchy inclusions and characteristic-zero strictness), I, and J. The claims include coalgebraic rounding, algebraic and coalgebraic amenability, Hopf-module quotients, cleft extensions, group and Lie applications, and augmentation-associated graded amenability. Every selected claim is proved without unformalized literature inputs or project-local axioms. Theorem D, the equivalence form of E, and arbitrary-characteristic strictness in H remain in the library but are excluded from the submission.
entries.title: Amenability of Lie, group and Hopf algebras

entries.abstract: The kissing number of Euclidean 3-space is 12: at most twelve unit balls with disjoint interiors touch a given unit ball, and twelve do. The upper bound follows Musin's extension of the Delsarte linear-programming method. The Delsarte machinery on the sphere (positive-definite zonal kernels up to degree 9 and the LP bound, which by itself gives only 13) is built from scratch, since Mathlib has no spherical harmonics. The lower bound is the cuboctahedron.
entries.title: kissing-number-lean

entries.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the multiplicative group K× modulo the field-norm subgroup N_{L/K}(L×) is isomorphic as a topological group to Gal(L/K). The registered declaration is the finite norm-quotient form of local reciprocity proved in the included ClassFieldTheory development. Stronger compatibility, normalization and existence results in that development are documented separately and are not part of the compared declaration.
entries.title: Local class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2

entries.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the idèle class group C_K modulo the image of the idèle-class norm from C_L is isomorphic as a topological multiplicative group to Gal(L/K). The Challenge defines the norm as the determinant on the relative adèle algebra and descends it through principal idèles; the included ClassFieldTheory development supplies the proof of the resulting reciprocity theorem.
entries.title: Global class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2

entries.abstract: Erdős problem #1220 (erdosproblems.com/1220; Erdős–Hajnal 1971): let λ be a singular cardinal such that both λ and cf(λ) are ℵ₀-inaccessible (μ^ℵ₀ < κ for all μ < κ); does λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² hold?  This formalization settles the question as asked on erdosproblems.com in the negative sense "not provable": ZFC does not prove that every such λ satisfies λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² (erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220)), i.e. there is a model of ZFC with a singular λ, λ and cf(λ) ℵ₀-inaccessible, and λ ↛ (λ, ℵ₁)².  Shelah and Stanley (Sh:258, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 36 (1987)) showed that a negative answer is consistent with ZFC.  This project formalizes that consistency result: the comparator target erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220) is stated for literally the same first-order theory ZFC, language and ZFSet interpretation as elliotglazer/erdos501's comparator challenge (imported from its statement module Erdos501.FOL.Statement), together with a faithfulness theorem erdos1220_sentence_faithful: in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence Erdos1220 holds iff the Mathlib-level statement Erdos1220.Problem1220 holds.  The witness is the ground-model singular strong-limit cardinal λ = ℶ_{𝔠⁺} (cf λ = 𝔠⁺; λ and cf λ are ℵ₀-inaccessible without any deep cardinal-arithmetic input), not ℵ_{𝔠⁺}.  The forcing is the Shelah–Stanley §3 forcing, formalized as block-preserving, block-covering histories of basic conditions (weak extension order), with the μ⁺-strategic closure (hence μ-distributivity) and the (2^μ)⁺-chain condition proved in ZFC without GCH (Δ-system lemma for (2^μ)⁺ sets of size ≤ μ, blueprint counting (2^μ)^μ = 2^μ).  In the Boolean-valued model of its regular-open algebra (built with the Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch vendored by erdos501) the hypotheses on λ are preserved, the generic colouring of [λ]² has neither a red homogeneous set of size λ nor a blue homogeneous set of size ℵ₁, and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns this into a two-valued model of ZFC satisfying ¬Erdos1220.  Both targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and pass the Lean comparator.  Only the negative direction is claimed: independence (consistency of a positive answer) is NOT claimed.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #1220 in Lean 4: the affirmative statement is not provable in ZFC

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of Schmidt's Subspace Theorem and the theory beneath it, following Bombieri–Gubler, Heights in Diophantine Geometry (Chapters 1–7), and Schmidt's route in general. Two libraries, sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. ArithmeticHeights builds heights of points, polynomials, matrices and linear subspaces, Northcott and Kronecker, Minkowski's second theorem, Siegel's lemma and the Bombieri–Vaaler theorems. DiophantineApproximation builds on it Roth's theorem over a number field with several places (and Ridout, the p-adic form, targets at infinity, moving targets), the geometry of numbers of approximation domains, and the Subspace Theorem: parametric, with coefficients in K, with algebraic coefficients, for S-integral points, and in Vojta's general-position form. It then proves the applications — Schmidt's simultaneous approximation, a transcendence criterion, unit equations, decomposable-form, Thue–Mahler, hyperelliptic and norm-form equations, the Corvaja–Zannier gcd bound — and Evertse's quantitative steps: systems of inequalities, the gap principles, the count of small solutions, and the passage from height intervals to subspaces. Twenty-six headline statements are compared: seven forms of Siegel's lemma and Bombieri–Vaaler, seven of Roth's theorem, seven of the Subspace Theorem, and five of Evertse's counting of the subspaces.
entries.title: Heights, Siegel's lemma, Roth's theorem and the Subspace Theorems in Lean

entries.abstract:
A countable domain R that is a left PCI ring (every cyclic left module not isomorphic to R is injective) and a left V-ring (every simple left module is injective), but is not right Ore, not a right PCI ring and not a right V-ring. Consequently the opposite ring of R is a right PCI ring that is not left PCI.
This answers in the negative the question of Faith (1973), Cozzens and Faith (Simple Noetherian Rings, 1975) and Damiano (1979) whether every right PCI ring is left PCI, and the question, going back to Cozzens and Faith (1975), whether a left V-domain must be a right V-domain.
The ring is an Ore extension K[t; σ, δ] over a free field K (Cohn's universal field of fractions of a free algebra over the rationals) with a non-surjective endomorphism σ, built by iteratively adjoining free solutions of the pseudo-linear equations that govern divisibility of the cyclic modules R/Rf.
The mathematics, the accompanying paper and the Lean code were produced by AI models (Anthropic's Claude) at a human's direction; no human expert has checked the mathematics.
entries.title: A left PCI left V-domain that is not right PCI and not a right V-domain

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the relative consistency of ZFC + CH together with the following assertion. There is a countably saturated elementary extension of the natural-number arithmetic structure of cardinality aleph one; all such set-sized presentations are isomorphic; and no such presentation is ordinal definable. The class is defined without parameters. Removing CH from the asserted theory gives a consistent negative answer to MathOverflow question 382009 about definability up to isomorphism versus an ordinal-definable copy. Every notion in the final sentence is internal to the first-order model of set theory.
entries.title: definable-saturated

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, on top of Mathlib, of the classical function theory of several complex variables on open subsets of finite-dimensional complex normed spaces, with values in complex Banach spaces wherever the statements allow. The compared statements cover: Cauchy's integral formula on polydiscs, Osgood's lemma, the equivalence of holomorphy and analyticity, the Cauchy-Riemann equations, Cauchy estimates, the identity theorem, the maximum modulus principle, holomorphic dependence of integrals and the Cauchy-Pompeiu identity; the theorems of Weierstrass, Montel and Vitali and an estimate for holomorphic L^p classes; the holomorphic inverse and implicit mapping theorems; Reinhardt domains, logarithmic convexity, the characterization of convergence domains of power series, Laurent expansion, and continuation from Reinhardt and circular domains; Hartogs-Taylor expansion, Hartogs' continuity theorem, Hartogs' theorem on separate analyticity, removability of isolated singularities, the two Riemann extension theorems and Hartogs' extension theorem for compact holes; elementary analytic sets and their regular points; the local ring of analytic germs, Weierstrass division and preparation, and the Noetherian and unique factorization properties of the germ ring; injective holomorphic maps, Cartan's uniqueness theorem, linearity of biholomorphisms of circular domains, transitivity of the automorphisms of the ball and the inequivalence of ball and polydisc; holomorphic hulls, domains of holomorphy, Thullen's lemma, the Cartan-Thullen theorem and Bochner's tube theorem; subharmonic and plurisubharmonic functions, the Levi form, pseudoconvexity of domains of holomorphy, Levi's theorem and local peak functions; Runge domains and polynomial hulls. All results are classical; none is claimed to be new.
entries.title: Several complex variables: local theory, Hartogs phenomena, Weierstrass theory, domains of holomorphy and pseudoconvexity

entries.abstract: We prove permutation realization for every admissible binary X-ray profile whose rank deviations from the odd staircase lie in [-2, 2], at every order and without a bound on density slack. We also prove the one-sided families with all deviations at least -1 or all deviations at most 1, with at least 2^u realizations, where u counts positive or negative deviations respectively. For n >= 1, if a label multiset L is realizable at order n, then Q(L) = {3, 2n+1} multiset-union (L+2) is realizable at order n+2. If every source label lies in [2, 2n-2], then h(L) <= h(Q(L)), where h counts permutation realizations. Repeated source labels are allowed. A least-order counterexample to the unrestricted conjecture must have first deviation at least 3 or last deviation at most -3. The unrestricted conjecture remains open.
entries.title: Constructive families and an extension theorem for binary permutation X-rays

entries.abstract: For a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q > 2, this development evaluates a sum of three normalized Haar integrals of an explicit eight-term Weyl kernel defined from valuations of entries and two-by-two minors of a concrete 4 by 4 matrix. It proves measurability and Bochner integrability on the natural damped range, an explicit rational evaluation in the undamped interior, principal Abel convergence, and the whole signed special Abel limit at delta = plus or minus q^(-1/2). The Satake parameters are unitary and avoid the stated Weyl walls; the special quotient also excludes parameters equal to its sign. The proof assembles all fifty infinite valuation regions with the source Haar normalizations. This adapts local calculations in Paul, Pitale, Saha and Schmidt's Fourier–Jacobi period paper. Identification of the explicit kernel with the paper's independently defined spherical coefficient and the full period identity are not claimed. The positive special-sign product is identically zero. No undamped special-endpoint integrability or extension to exceptional parameter walls is asserted.
entries.title: Explicit Fourier–Jacobi Haar-core evaluation and Abel limits

entries.abstract: Let J be the split Albert algebra over a field k of characteristic zero, the 27-dimensional Jordan algebra of 3 by 3 Hermitian matrices over the split octonions, with trace tr. A frame is an ordered triple of trace-one idempotents summing to 1. Three frames E, F, K carry 54 natural invariants under the group G of all unital k-linear bijections of J preserving its Jordan product: the pair traces tr(eᵢ∘fⱼ), tr(fⱼ∘kₗ), tr(kₗ∘eᵢ) and the triple traces tr(eᵢ∘(fⱼ∘kₗ)). This Lean 4 development proves that these traces do not generate all rational invariants of three frames, and that adjoining one additional invariant suffices: the field of G-invariant rational functions on the variety of frame triples is a quadratic extension H(d) of the field H generated by the 54 traces, where d = tr(W∘(W∘W)), W = x∘(y∘z) − y∘(x∘z), x = e₂ − e₀, y = f₂ − f₀, z = k₂ − k₀. The development also proves that the variety of frame triples is irreducible, that the coordinate algebra used is the standard split Albert algebra, that d is not in H, and that every invariant is uniquely a + b·d with a, b in H. The ambiguity occurs over ℚ: two explicit frame triples have identical 54 traces and d = −2591357/62208 and −1782559/62208, and no ℚ-linear automorphism of J combined with any of the 1,296 relabellings of frames and idempotents carries one to the other. The proved endpoints use only the permitted axiom dependencies propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice; a Python script rechecks the example in exact arithmetic.
entries.title: Rational invariants of three frames in the split Albert algebra: a Lean formalization

entries.abstract: For finite games with player-specific action types, a valid independent product distribution is a correlated equilibrium exactly when its mixed profile is Nash. The correlated-equilibrium set is nonempty, compact, and convex when every player's action type is nonempty. For every positive finite horizon, cumulative external-regret and swap-regret bounds give corresponding approximate coarse-correlated and correlated equilibria of the empirical distribution. The development also proves equivalence with conditional obedience inequalities, arbitrary mixed-deviation sufficiency, and extension-by-zero correspondence for restricted legal actions. An exact per-recommendation certificate characterizes approximate correlated equilibrium without loss in its error budget and directly certifies empirical play from cumulative recommendation gains.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Finite correlated equilibria and regret certificates
